title: Suspect arrested over Kahawatta gem businessman’s murder
byline: Police have taken a suspect into custody in connection with the murder of a gem businessman in Kahawatta.

title: Trump urges countries seeking oil to go to Strait of Hormuz and ’just take it’
byline: President Donald Trump on Tuesday urged countries that did not help in the U.S.-Israeli strikes on ​Iran to buy American oil and go to ‌the Strait of Hormuz and ’’just TAKE it.’’

title: Market ends mixed amid volatility and index rebalancing pressure
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange experienced a highly volatile session on 31st March 2026, with the market oscillating between gains and losses throughout the day. Early optimism was supported by positive global cues following updates from the U.S. President regarding developments in the ongoing geopolitical situation, which initially lifted investor sentiment and pushed the market into positive territory.

title: Sri Lanka Coast Guard rescues 18 tourists from drowning in March
byline: The Sri Lanka Coast Guard successfully rescued 18 local and foreign tourists from drowning during lifesaving operations carried out across several coastal areas in March 2026.

title: Discussions with electricity trade unions progress successfully
byline: A key discussion between trade union representatives of the Ceylon Electricity Board and chairpersons of newly established state-owned electricity companies was held yesterday (30) at the Labour Ministry, under the patronage of Labour Deputy Minister Mahinda Jayasinghe.

title: Russian deputy foreign minister arrives in Sri Lanka
byline: Andrey Rudenko, Russia’s Deputy Foreign Minister, arrived in Sri Lanka today on an official visit.

title: China bans entombing cremated remains in empty flats
byline: Chinese authorities have banned entombing cremated remains in cheap apartments, a practice that had gained popularity as mourners took advantage of the subdued housing market to dodge rising funeral costs.

title: Johnston Fernando’s sons granted bail
byline: The Negombo High Court today (31) granted bail to four suspects, including two sons of former Minister Johnston Fernando, who had been remanded over the alleged misuse of a Lanka Sathosa lorry.

title: CPC allows fuel for all vehicles tomorrow under QR system
byline: The Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC) announced that fuel will be available tomorrow (April 1) for both odd- and even-numbered vehicles under the existing QR quota system.

title: Cabinet approves fuel allowances for ministers, MPs, and public officials
byline: The Cabinet of Ministers has approved fuel allowances for Ministers, Members of Parliament, and government officers, calculated based on fuel prices as of March 1, 2026.

title: Unlawful garbage dumping: Supreme Court rules authorities violated Meethotamulla residents’ rights
byline: The Supreme Court today declared that several key state authorities, including the Colombo Municipal Council (CMC), the Kolonnawa Urban Council and the Urban Development Authority, had violated the Fundamental Rights of residents in the Meethotamulla area through unlawful conduct and improper garbage disposal practices.

title: Australia investigates tech giants over social media ban breaches
byline: Australia threatened on Tuesday to sue social media ​giants for allegedly flouting a ban on under-16s, as its internet regulator disclosed it is investigating some of ‌the biggest platforms for suspected non-compliance with the world-first measure.

title: Cabinet nod to import rice amid Samba shortage
byline: The Cabinet has decided to grant permits to import rice varieties similar to Samba and Keeri Samba, in a move aimed at addressing the current shortage in the country.

title: International Dhamma Programme webinar scheduled for Full Moon Poya Day
byline: The International Dhamma Programme will host a special online session on Full Moon Poya Day, Wednesday, April 1, 2026, inviting participants worldwide to join via Zoom.

title: At least 70 people killed and 30 injured in Haiti gang attack
byline: At least 70 people have been killed and 30 injured during an attack in Haiti’s breadbasket Artibonite region, significantly more than official estimates, a human rights group has said.

title: Sri Lankan Rupee slides further against USD
byline: The Sri Lankan rupee continued its decline against the US dollar across commercial banks today (31), with the selling rate holding steady at Rs. 318.

title: Dr. Madurangi Ariyasinghe cleared by court to lead SLCEP
byline: The Commercial High Court of Colombo has delivered a landmark judgement clearing the way for Dr. Madurangi Ariyasinghe, Consultant Emergency Physician, to assume office as the first female President of the Sri Lanka College of Emergency Physicians (SLCEP).

title: Food prices rise at eateries from tonight
byline: Food prices at eateries across the country will be increased with effect from midnight today (March 31), following a decision by the All-Island Canteen and Restaurant Owners’ Association, citing rising operational costs.

title: Tharanga tops world list with record javelin throw
byline: Sri Lanka’s rising javelin star Rumesh Tharanga produced a stunning performance to set a new national record with a throw of 89.37 metres at the Champions Track & Field Meet held at the Mahinda Rajapaksa Stadium on Saturday.

title: Record entrepreneur loans expected in 2026: Sunil Handunneththi
byline: Industry and Entrepreneurship Development Minister Sunil Handunneththi, announced that 2026 will witness the highest number of loans granted to entrepreneurs in recent history, as part of the government’s efforts to strengthen the industrial sector.

title: Accused energy minister should resign without waiting for opposition: Namal
byline: Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) National Organiser Namal Rajapaksa has called for the resignation of the country’s accused Energy Minister, stating that such action should be taken without waiting for demands from the opposition.

title: CAA raids illegal fertilizer sale in Matara
byline: The Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) in Matara has conducted a special raid targeting the illegal sale of fertilizer, following a complaint received on March 30, 2026.

title: Man nabbed at BIA for attempting to smuggle protected plant species to China
byline: A foreign national was arrested at Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA) this morniong (31) while attempting to smuggle a stock of the protected plant Kotala Himbutu (Salacia reticulata) out of the country, Customs officials said.

title: Israel passes death penalty law for Palestinians convicted of lethal attacks
byline: Israel’s parliament passed a law on Monday making death by hanging a default sentence for Palestinians convicted in military courts of deadly attacks, fulfilling a pledge by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s far-right allies.

title: Parliamentary Committee mulls immediate plan on ash disposal from Norochcholai
byline: In the wake of controversy over substandard coal imports to Sri Lanka, a parliamentary Committee has instructed officials to immediately prepare a plan for the environmentally friendly disposal of ash emitted from the Norochcholai Lakvijaya Power Plant.

title: Oil down 1% after report says Trump open to ending campaign against Iran
byline: Oil prices reversed course in Asian trading on ‌Tuesday, paring earlier gains, following a report that U.S. President Donald Trump told aides he is willing to end the Iran war without reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Study finds high mercury in women’s hair near Puttalam lagoon
byline: A disturbing new study has intensified concerns over environmental pollution and public health in Sri Lanka due to combustion of low-quality coal, revealing that women with no occupational exposure to mercury have recorded alarmingly high levels of the toxic metal in their hair.

title: Giant oil tanker off Dubai hit by Iranian strike
byline: Iran attacked and set ablaze a fully loaded crude oil tanker off Dubai on Monday, ​as President Donald Trump warned the U.S. would obliterate Iran’s energy plants and oil wells if it does not open the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Gem trader found dead in mine pit in Kahawatta
byline: The body of a 61-year-old gem trader who had gone missing in the Kahawatta area has been discovered inside a mine pit in Neelagama.

title: Pakistan cricket star handed massive $105k fine for deleted social media post
byline: Pakistan fast bowler Naseem Shah has been hit with a massive AU$105,000 fine for a deleted social media post that appeared to criticise Punjab’s chief minister Maryam Nawaz.

title: Three teenagers charged with murder after girl stabbed to death in Leeds
byline: Three teenagers have been charged with the murder of a 16-year-old who was stabbed to death in Leeds.

title: Three million Indian officials to begin counting world’s largest population
byline: More than 3 ​million Indian officials are to spend a year counting every single ‌person in the world’s most populous nation, a mammoth task delayed in part by the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Russia, Sri Lanka discuss strengthening parliamentary ties
byline: Parliamentary leader of the ruling United Russia party in the State Duma, Vladimir Vasilyev, met with Sri Lanka’s Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development and Leader of the House, Bimal Rathnayake, during a meeting held at the State Duma.

title: Two disused train compartments catch fire near Galle station
byline: Two out-of-service train compartments parked near the Galle Railway Station caught fire today.

title: Sri Lankan injured in Dubai Shrapnel incident
byline: Four individuals including a Sri Lankan in Dubai have sustained injuries caused by falling debris from a successful interception.

title: Supreme Court revives indictments against ex-Minister Tennakoon
byline: The Supreme Court today set aside the judgment delivered by the Court of Appeal in 2020, which quashed the operation of indictments filed against former Minister Janaka Bandara Tennakoon before the Kandy High Court over an alleged murder committed in 1999.

title: Sri Lanka to offer free tourist visas for 39 countries
byline: Sri Lanka will introduce a six-month programme granting free tourist visas to passport holders from 39 selected countries in a bid to boost the country’s tourism industry.
